body: New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 4A defines living alone. A single person is living alone only if the person occupies qualifying accommodation as the person's principal residence and does not share that residence with any person 18 years old or older except an exempt 18-year-old dependent child or a temporary visitor who stays less than 13 weeks in any period of 26 weeks.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 7 provides that every person is entitled to receive New Zealand superannuation who attains the age of 65 years, but a person is not entitled for a period for which the person has made an election to be entitled to weekly compensation rather than New Zealand superannuation. The rule is subject to Part 1 of the Act, the Social Security Act 2018, and the Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act 2018.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 8 requires ordinary residence in New Zealand on the date of application unless an overseas residence exception applies, and requires residence and presence since age 20 for a total-time requirement, including 10 years in New Zealand and the remaining time in New Zealand, the Cook Islands, Niue, or Tokelau. It also requires 5 years residence and presence since age 50 in any of those places. Section 8(4) sets the total-time table: on or before 30 June 1959 requires 10 years; 1 July 1959 to 30 June 1961 requires 11 years; 1 July 1961 to 30 June 1963 requires 12 years; 1 July 1963 to 30 June 1965 requires 13 years; 1 July 1965 to 30 June 1967 requires 14 years; 1 July 1967 to 30 June 1969 requires 15 years; 1 July 1969 to 30 June 1971 requires 16 years; 1 July 1971 to 30 June 1973 requires 17 years; 1 July 1973 to 30 June 1975 requires 18 years; 1 July 1975 to 30 June 1977 requires 19 years; and on or after 1 July 1977 requires 20 years. This encoding represents June as month 6 for the 30 June cutoff dates.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 11 provides that New Zealand superannuation commences on the date the applicant becomes entitled to receive it or the date the department receives the application, whichever is later, subject to section 317 of the Social Security Act 2018.
New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 12 provides that the rate of New Zealand superannuation payable to a person is the appropriate rate specified in Schedule 1.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 Schedule 1 Part 1 sets ordinary New Zealand superannuation rates before deduction of tax from 1 April 2026: $647.37 a week to a single person living alone, $595.57 a week to a single person not living alone, and $492.14 a week to a person who is married, in a civil union, or in a de facto relationship. The Part also states a hospital-rate net amount after tax code M, which is outside this ordinary-rate slice.
